name: PMS5003 particulate matter (PM2.5) sensor
description: Plantower laser-scattering dust sensor reporting PM1.0, PM2.5 and PM10 mass concentration (µg/m³, 0-500 effective, >=1000 max) and particle counts per 0.1 L over a 9600-baud UART (3.3 V logic). Needs 4.5-5.5 V for its fan, draws up to 100 mA. Sold as: Adafruit PM2.5 Air Quality Sensor and Breadboard Adapter Kit - PMS5003 (#3686), 8-pin 2.54 mm adapter: VCC, GND, SET, RXD, TXD, RST, NC, NC.
eli5: A little fan pulls air past a laser and counts the dust and smoke specks, then tells your board how dirty the air is.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 5 V (4.5-5.5 V): the fan needs 5 V

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground (the metal case is also ground)

pins.name: SET
pins.description: Sleep control, 3.3 V logic, pulled up inside: high/open = run, low = sleep

pins.name: RXD
pins.description: Sensor serial input (3.3 V logic): wire to the board's UART TX; only needed to send commands

pins.name: TXD
pins.description: Sensor serial output (3.3 V logic, 9600 baud): wire to the board's UART RX

pins.name: RST
pins.description: Reset, active low, pulled up inside; leave open if unused

supplierQuery: PMS5003 PM2.5 sensor with breadboard adapter
buildNotes: Power VCC from 5 V (the fan needs 4.5-5.5 V, up to 100 mA), but the data pins are 3.3 V logic: safe straight into an ESP32 or Pico; a 5 V Arduino needs a level shifter on RXD.
Cross the serial wires: sensor TXD -> board RX, sensor RXD -> board TX (RXD is only needed to send commands).

9600 baud 8N1. In active mode (power-up default) the sensor sends a 32-byte frame on its own: 0x42 0x4D, length 28, 13 big-endian words, then a 16-bit sum of the first 30 bytes. Resync on 0x42 0x4D and drop frames whose sum does not match.
Data 4-6 are PM1.0/PM2.5/PM10 'under atmospheric environment' (use these indoors/outdoors); data 1-3 are the CF=1 values meant for factory calibration.
Leave SET, RST and both NC pins unconnected unless you use them; SET low puts the fan to sleep. Readings need about 30 s after waking to settle.
Mount it at least 20 cm above the floor, keep the air inlet and outlet unobstructed, and keep the metal case away from other conductors (it is grounded).

example.code:
from machine import UART, Pin
from pms5003 import PMS5003

uart = UART({UART_ID}, baudrate=9600, tx=Pin({RXD}), rx=Pin({TXD}))
pms = PMS5003(uart)
while True:
    r = pms.read()
    print('PM1=%d PM2.5=%d PM10=%d' % (r['pm1_0'], r['pm2_5'], r['pm10']))

test.title: Reports the PM1.0, PM2.5 and PM10 set on the sliders

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading (1 difference(s) settled by a third reading with quoted evidence). Not yet tested on real hardware.
